claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a homogeneous, single-phase microstructure.
A calibrated post-deposition heat treatment can induce controlled nanoscale Cu segregation at grain boundaries.
The heat treatment can form coherent Cu-enriched intergranular films or precipitates.
Atomic diffusion at the operating temperature enables Cu atoms to segregate to grain boundaries.
The Cu-enriched intergranular phase increases grain-boundary cohesion.
The Cu-enriched intergranular phase impedes grain-boundary sliding under tribological stress.
The Cu-enriched intergranular phase suppresses dynamic recrystallization under tribological stress.
Suppression of grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recrystallization limits localized plastic deformation.
The Cu-enriched intergranular phase limits microcrack propagation under tribological stress.
An appropriately heat-treated coating will exhibit less microscopic plastic deformation than the as-deposited homogeneous coating.
An appropriately heat-treated coating will exhibit greater overall wear resistance than the as-deposited homogeneous coating.
Absent or excessively thick and embrittling Cu segregation will increase deformation relative to the optimized condition.
Absent or excessively thick and embrittling Cu segregation will increase wear relative to the optimized condition.
The predicted effects are expected to hold during sliding between 600 K and 800 K.
At lower temperatures, insufficient diffusion may limit Cu segregation.
At excessively high temperatures, coarsening or embrittlement may occur.
